title: Interpreter Access for Mobile Clinics and Street Medicine
summary: Plan interpreter coverage for mobile clinics and street medicine by route, with practical steps for weak signal, privacy, and follow-up.
body_markdown:
###


A mobile clinic coverage card should list the stop, common language requests, primary and backup connection methods, the location of a private space, and the person responsible for escalation. Update the card after route changes or a failed connection.


###


A phone interpreter needs a working voice connection, such as a tested phone line at a nearby site. If an outreach stop has no usable connection, plan on-site coverage or an alternate location under the team’s approved protocol.


###


Staff should pause the affected discussion, follow the team’s backup protocol, and resume from the last point the patient and clinician confirmed. Document any unresolved communication and who will handle the follow-up.


###


Mobile clinic teams should confirm the patient’s preferred written language, accessible format, and safe delivery channel before sending approved translated instructions. Use live interpretation when the patient needs to ask questions or clarify the plan.


###


An outreach team should test spoken language support, audio, connectivity, privacy, and the backup connection at the actual stop. Use the encounter type, patient preference, and local policy to decide which approved interpretation option fits.
